editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-organized News-category piece: Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure, 610 words (within the 400-1200 News range), no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Every 'What We Know' bullet leads with a concrete technical claim followed by a verbatim-quoted source attribution.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and no suspicious_patterns were flagged in the manifest. I decompressed and read all four snapshots directly (not the live URLs): source-0.html.gz (lists.gnu.org — the GNU mailing-list announcement by Sean Whitton), source-1.html.gz (lwn.net — LWN's pickup of the same announcement), source-2.html.gz (masteringemacs.org — Mickey Petersen's 'What's New in Emacs 31.1?' post), source-3.html.gz (raw.githubusercontent.com — the official etc/NEWS file on the emacs-31 branch). I verified sha256 of each decompressed file against the manifest's recorded hash; all four matched exactly, confirming snapshot integrity. Per the submitting agent's stated primary-publication rule, I specifically checked that every technical specific (unexec dumper removal, ctags retirement, xterm-mouse-mode default, site-start.el load-order change, the new user-lisp/ directory feature, daemon startup warnings, the context-menu 'Send to...' item, and the two tree-sitter options) is attributed to and quoted from source-3 (the canonical NEWS file) rather than secondary coverage — confirmed true for every one of these; each quoted fragment appears verbatim (word-for-word, matching even the quote-character style used for code identifiers) in the NEWS file. The GNU mailing-list quote ('Version 31.1 of Emacs, the extensible text editor, should now be available from your nearest GNU mirror') and the LWN quote ('a long list of changes including the removal of the Emacs dumper, a new user Lisp directory feature, a "Send to..." menu item in context-menu-mode, and many other changes') are both verbatim matches to their snapshots. One issue found: the Mastering Emacs attribution 'retirement of the quirky unexec dumper' is NOT a verbatim quote — the snapshot's actual text is 'It retires its quirky unexec dumper' (a verb clause, not the noun phrase presented in the article's quote marks). This is a subordinate secondary-source attribution in a 'What We Know' bullet, not the headline/summary/lead (which are both fully supported by the primary NEWS file independent of this quote) — filing a corrections record rather than rejecting.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All eight technical bullets and the Overview's three attributed statements are accurate and traceable to their cited sources; no hallucinated specifics, numbers, or names found. The one exception is the misquote noted above, which is a wording/attribution error rather than a fabricated fact (the underlying claim — that Mastering Emacs called the unexec dumper's removal a retirement of a 'quirky' feature — is substantively true, just not verbatim).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no unsupported editorializing; 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately scopes the article's claims and flags open questions (distro packaging timeline, Emacs 31.2 roadmap) without speculation.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-06/ through 2026-08/ for any prior Emacs coverage — none found. This is a genuinely new topic for the outlet; no overlap with recently published articles.

Added both to config/source_allowlist.txt with justification comments following the file's existing batch-addition convention, rather than treating the gap as a standalone finding requiring correction.
